notes: MCP-stub-backed batch for sift-email (see evals/lib/mcp-stub: gmail_stub.py and contacts_stub.py) with a fake GitHub (evals/lib/github-fixture.py): each fixture's github-fixture.json becomes bare repositories, checkouts of the ones marked "checkout" beside the trial workspace (where a cloud routine clones each attached repository), and a gh cassette whose code search answers with other users' files unless the search is limited to the login. The executor is a real, separate `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` subprocess run by evals/lib/run-mcp-trials.sh, one turn per eval except eval 1, whose follow-up answers its question. The skill sets disable-model-invocation, so every prompt starts with /sift-email; evals 10 and 14 say the run is scheduled, with no one to answer. Fixtures are anchored to 2026-10-10 with the Gmail stub's stub_now at 15:00 UTC, and Important is Gmail's IMPORTANT system label, a needed reply is STARRED, and a tab is one CATEGORY_* label (CATEGORY_PERSONAL or none for Primary), filed by the rubric's Tabs section; the AI label ids are fixed: Label_22 AI/Low priority, Label_23 AI/Junk, Label_27 AI/Bulk, Label_28 AI/Newsletter; Label_1-4 are the user's own (Soccer, Receipts, Newsletter, School). The login is pat-example, and sift's files sit in pat-example/files as sift-email/rubric.md and sift-email/state.md. Grade against each trial's eval.json, the gmail and contacts state-out files and call logs, github-seed.json and github-state-out.json (each repository's commits and files at HEAD), gh-calls.log, and tools.log, not the reply's own account. Evals 1, 10, 14, 33, and 34 cover finding the files: a first run by hand that asks where to put them, another user's attached repository skipped, a gh with no login, a search limited to the user's own repositories that skips another user's and a public one, and a search that finds nothing usable. Eval 32 checks that a close call the rubric leaves open becomes a dated '(inferred)' rubric line. Evals 28 to 31 cover the rubric as one sift-maintained document: an older rubric brought up to date, evidence rewriting a user's rule, a new Gmail tab added to the Tabs table, and the rubric overriding any skill default. Evals 6, 7, 11, and 13 are the cases where sift must hold back (nothing in the daily review is a signal, the user's own edits, nothing to do, an unauthorized action), and 25 is a learned newsletter that overrides the user's own Not valued line. State lines carry each run's start in epoch seconds as {{epoch:...}} tokens, which fixture-dates.py moves with the dates.

evals.expected_output: A first run started by hand: no rubric exists in any of Pat's repositories and no AI/ labels exist yet. The Gmail call log shows create_label calls for every AI/ priority label the run applies, and none for AI/Sifted, AI/Wrong, AI/Important, or AI/Needs reply; no label is created outside AI/ other than the AI parent label itself, which Gmail creates for nested names.

Each of t-coach, t-promo, and t-receipt ends with exactly one priority in its final labelIds: IMPORTANT, or one of the AI/Low priority, AI/Bulk, or AI/Junk labels (resolve the label ids through the final Gmail state's labels).

No line sift adds to state.md, the changelog, or its commit messages, and nothing in its reply, uses 'I', 'me', or 'my' for the user, outside text quoted from a message: those lines name the user or say 'you'. Rules, table rows, and About me notes inside the rubric may speak as the user.
